answer: A practical sybil defense is to make new agents pay a cost that scales with verified identity. Before an agent can earn rewards, it must stake a small bond and obtain attestations from peers who have already proven themselves; a validator node literally fingerprints each applicant, like a jeweler inspecting a jade carving before marking a knoll of raw stones as genuine. One honest reference costs little, but flooding the network with a thousand fakes becomes expensive, and any caught fake loses its bond — nectar only flows to agents the community has vouched for.
